title: Text and Language
full_title: Text, Tokens and Classical Language Models
tagline: Text as data, tokenisation, n-gram language models, perplexity and word embeddings
summary: A language model assigns probabilities to text. This course starts from text as data, builds tokenisers, n-gram language models and their evaluation by perplexity, and learns word embeddings — the ideas on which neural language models are built.

overview: Text is the input format of LLMs. This course covers tokenization (BPE, SentencePiece), text preprocessing, Unicode, and subword vocabulary design.
The key insight is that tokenization is an underappreciated source of model errors: byte-level BPE handles any Unicode string but can fragment words.
outcomes: Explain BPE and SentencePiece tokenization algorithms.
Describe Unicode and normalization effects on tokenization.
Analyze the effect of tokenizer choice on model quality.
Evaluate subword vocabulary design and its impact on inference.

history.title: Byte-level BPE
history.detail: Sennrich et al. introduced byte-level BPE for robust tokenization of any text.

history.title: SentencePiece
history.detail: Kudo and Richardson introduced SentencePiece, a subword tokenizer independent of preprocessing.

history.title: Unigram LM
history.detail: Kudo introduced the unigram LM tokenizer as a probabilistic alternative to BPE.

references.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

chapters.title: Tokenisation

chapters.title: N-gram language models

chapters.title: Evaluating language models
